tips.comment: The Warren Greatrex-trained Amor Cordis has run well without winning and is an 8-race maiden. However, this Class 6 handicap looks like a good race for the 3-year-old Havana Gold gelding to get off the mark with the son of the trainer, Edward Greatrex, in the saddle.

Ruling Master is a 3-year-old gelding trained by Jamie Osbourne. He is dropped down significantly in trip, and the stiff uphill finish should bring out the best of his ability. 0-10 wins and posted a career-high RPR of 73 and runs off 64 today, so looks fairly well treated. Saffie can land a hat-trick.
Callout didn't handle heavy ground last time according to his trainer. Back on the firmer ground today, this former CD winner can easily bounce back from his poor run last time.

The trainer has had an unusually quiet season but there are signs that the tide is turning now and he's going to have some very well handicapped horses on his hands. This horse has yet to place in 7 runs but has shown in his 4th of 12 in a maiden that he could be very well in here off 64. The horse was around horses rated much higher than this mark and that maiden has produced a stack of winners. He gets the booking of Jason Watson too for just the 2nd time and he was only beaten 2 lengths on the horse for his only previous ride on him.

Play Me showed clear signs of returning to form when finishing a close third at Salisbury, running well off a mark of 60. With prior placing experience at this distance and on similar going, Play Me looks set to build on recent improvement.
Blue Empress likes this distance best and good ground conditions. I'm expecting a big run. The yard performs well at Brighton and has a good strike rate. E/w prospect.

It's not ideal that this horse is drawn out wide and is returning from a rest but, he's still very unexposed on this surface so it's difficult to rule out some improvement yet. Top jockey is booked, the horse will be given every chance by this jockey. Very small each-way tip for Manton Road

BROADHAVEN BOY likes it at Brighton on good to firm ground, expecially over the minmum trip, but he can get six furlongs. He's back down to his last winning mark of 55, and I suppose the big question is... can he translate his five furlong form over this slightly longer trip, and to me, it's obvious.
Won well on debut at Lingfield over 6f 13 days ago by 2.5L going away at the business end so today's extra 1f could bring some further improvement despite carrying the penalty .

3-year-old filly sired by New Bay has some decent form to her name, running a good 3rd last time out here on standard going. Breeding suggests she will be okay on the slower surface today, and at least she is proven at the track. Up against a couple of penalized last time out winners has helped her price, and I make her a decent bet and my NAP today.
Darn Hot Time was worn down right on the line over 7f at Wolverhampton last time when a head 2nd to Call Me Betty. Getting weight from the previous winners, she should go close.

Miss Chester looks very overpriced here. Won last time out when showing a lot of improvement, and if that improvement continues, she could run a big race at bigger prices again. One to watch at decent e/w value.
Jabaara is in excellent form with a top 3 finish in 7 of the last 9 races including 3 wins. I also expect a win for Jabaara in the race today.

Cloud Cover returned from a break in a C2F handicap and was at the back of the pack. I am expecting the return to listed company, in which she won in France in December, could see a revival now second up after wind surgery.
Last ran nearly a year ago when 2nd at Newmarket. If fully tuned up, must have a great chance. My NB selection.

Miss Information is a 4-year-old filly trained by Andrew Balding. She has 5 wins out of 15 on turf and out of 1 on AW but has improved significantly since that AW run. She won the 23-runner Kensington Palace Stakes handicap at Royal Ascot, posting a career-high RPR of 104. The next six home had also all won on the AW. She is also related to three individual winners, two of which won on the AW: Newscaster and Lead Story, so she has the pedigree to figure on AW tonight. Upped to listed class for the first time, it's more of a challenge, but her dam won a listed race at Nottingham and placed in a Group 3 at the Curragh. Miss Information represents Balding, who has picked up 16 winners in recent weeks. Balding plundered races in July 24, landing a haul of 27 winners. Given Oisin Murphy has ridden 424 wins for Andrew Balding, combined a good source of winners.

A typical race at Chester where the ones tapped for toe at the start. Ralf Beckett's runner could never get going from mid-division until they straightened up, and it was going the best of all but too late. I'll chance again under Rossa Ryan.

A Chester winner in July last year before going over to France when making 3rd at Longchamp. Can be forgiven for the recent 5th place as it was the first run of the year. The ability may arise again now.

THELMA'S ANGEL appeared to get squeezed out at a vital stage when racing in the recent Kensington Palace Stakes at Royal Ascot. Her finishing position when midfield does not tell the full story and although apparently something to find on official ratings she is improving and makes each-way appeal.

I’m backing Powdering, the 5-year-old Ribchester mare trained by Michael Herrington, in tomorrow’s Bet365 Queen Charlotte Fillies’ Stakes (Listed, 7f Polytrack). While she disappointed when finishing 10th of 13 at York on 13 June (sent off around 10/1) , her winter form tells a different story??'most notably landing back-to-back wins at Southwell in February and March over 6??'7f . That run style??'tracking the pace before peaking late??'ought to suit Chelmsford’s long straight.
She’s been freshened up since that York run, now stepping back into Polytrack where she’s proven effective, handling both the turn of pace and surface well . With a likely strong early gallop from the field and the recent confidence from AW victories, Powdering has every chance to fire a bold late challenge.
The field lines up as a competitive 11??'runner, and with her current mark around 83 she carries solid each-way value??'more so back on her favoured surface. If she can recapture her Southwell rhythm, she’ll be bang there in the closing stages.
Belgravian won going away on handicap debut by 2L last month, which makes me think today's step up to 1m5f could suit and defy that 4 lbs rise.

Deep Water Bay is in stall 4, running off a mark of 75, which looks very fair after recent good form. He won well by 2 lengths off 59 over 12 furlongs at Wolverhampton two runs ago and was second last time, beaten 2 lengths off 65, where he looked a bit too keen early. Trainer Mark Prescott and jockey Laurie Morris have 19 runs together with a 5% win rate and 26% place rate. The stall is decent, and the pace should be strong, which will help him settle better this time. He tends to race a bit keen, so a good pace is ideal for him to settle mid-pack before making a strong finish. Deep Water Bay looks a good win chance with his current mark and trainer form.
An Bradan Feasa won at Catterick in April. He followed it up with another two decent runs. Now further upped in trip, he could figure again and hit the frame.
Not really bred for this sort of trip, but the stable probably knows better. Had three minor runs to date and now makes a handicap debut and gets weight from most of the field. Interesting.
Failed in his bid for the double at Lingfield when beaten favorite, but mark remains unchanged and interesting now on a longer trip.

Perrine - bred well out of Raven's Pass, a cast-off from the Gosden yard. She may have shown some ability on the AW, placing 3rd at Kempton. Connections will try her here for the first time and also give her a spin up in distance. Small yard but have had winners recently and have booked a jockey who gets his fair share here, running at 15%.

Almaty Star looks to be the favoured Cowell horse here and also looks to be the only horse that has got consistent form in running at the front, with the majority happy to sit off this. Hollie Doyle may be able to get in front, put on the brakes and kick on at the right time to win here.

Monsieur Beaulieu ran well when 2nd from an outer draw over course and distance back in February, his only recent try over the minimum distance. But with a good start from stall 1 here, he has every chance of a win.
Finished runner-up in his last 3 starts, the last 2 over 6 furlongs. He is a former course and distance winner and should welcome the drop in trip.

Fantasy Master is in stall number 2 which is ideal for him as he likes to sit handy and just off the pace. He was beaten 5 lengths over 7f here last time, so dropping back to 6 is very much in his favour. He has 4 wins and 8 places from 26 starts at this distance giving him a 15% win rate and 46% place rate over the trip, and he has won over this course before. His current handicap mark of 79 is not lenient but within my reach, especially as he won back to back races off similar ratings last autumn. Ray Dawson keeps the ride and Darryll Holland’s runners often go well when freshened up like this. Has a solid record in cheekpieces and now drawn low with pace to track, he is not one to rule out. Each way shout if things fall his way

Both career wins have come over today's course and distance. Excellent effort when just one length back in third here last time out behind the re-opposing Ziggy's Missile. Four pounds better off with that rival today and looks a value bet for each-way purposes at least with top young jockey Billy Loughnane taking the ride.

A beaten favourite over this trip at Lingfield on turf last time out. It may welcome the return to this track and trip, having run well over course and distance on penultimate start when running on well inside the final furlong. Finished 4th of 8, beaten by 1.5 lengths off a pound higher mark.
Bamburgh looked strong in the last race with a second place. In this field, I give Bamburgh a good chance to grab the win.

TRIBAL WISDOM looks way overpriced at 16/1. Last time out, in a C5 contest, he was unable to concede 10lb to the winner and 5lb to the runner-up at Salisbury. Time before that, he was outclassed from a poor high draw in a C3 event at Lingfield. More his level this evening. All three career wins have come on the all-weather.

Kitaro Kich won here back in March off a 77 and followed up with a decent C3 second off an 81. Although the next two runs on turf were a bit duff, I think the return here back on the AW and on an 81 could be worth an EW.
Went out like a light 12 days ago. Seemingly only a minor issue and he returns to the track quickly. Paddy Bradley has won on him before and he has an excellent draw.

Con Te Partiro is in stall 1 and a mark of 90, which looks fair and below his last winning mark, giving him a good chance today. He was third at Yarmouth last time over a similar trip, beaten 5 lengths. Trainer Richard Spencer and jockey Hollie Doyle have 40 runs together with a 3% win rate and 15% place rate. He has course and distance experience with a place on this track and has won twice at this distance. He handles polytrack well and performs best wearing cheekpieces and a tongue strap, which he wears today. Stall 1 is handy for him, and with a decent pace expected, he should get a good tow into the race and finish strongly. Big chance here, IMHO.
Blindedbythelights looks capable of running a good race here. Form has been franked since losing out by a short head last time out. Step up in trip looks to suit so should be in the mix again.
Trouville shaped well when narrowly beaten here last time despite a slow start. Now steps up in trip, which should suit his pedigree. Progressive profile, top jockey booked. Big run expected.

ANZAC DAY appears to have sound claims in a competitive looking staying handicap. Already aimed higher by ace trainer Andrew Balding and tonight's new trip seems likely to in unlock further progress. Possibly the best and most realistic value from this field.

Was asked to compete at Group level in some decent staying races last season but has found life a lot easier returned to handicap company on his starts following a 5-month break. Only just failed to land a race at Goodwood two starts ago and was a close-up 12th of 20 at Royal Ascot last time from a slightly higher mark. Looks a really strong player here over slightly shorter in a first-time tongue tie and returning to the AW for the first time since November 2023.

A proven stayer who ran a big race off 84 when third at Goodwood last time out. Drops to a winnable mark here, has strong AW form, and Hollie Doyle takes over in the saddle - a significant booking which says the yard have strong opinions on this horse. Looks well handicapped on past exploits and handles the trip with no concerns. Big EV+ price.

An open-looking staying handicap where 12/1 shot Surrey Fire appeals. He ran well here last time, and the step up in trip today should help. He has dropped again in the handicap. That was also his first run in a while, so he should be fitter today.

This 7lb claiming apprentice is hugely promising and was impressive when hacking up on his only previous run on the horse. The horse was then sent off favorite over this C&D where Cieran Fallon gave this horse a poor ride when slowly away and then meeting all sorts of trouble in running before only being beaten less than 2 lengths. She's 2lb higher now, but the jockey's 7lb claim more than makes up for that, and hopefully, he'll ping the horse out and make up for that effort over C&D.

Finbars Lad has not won since June 2023 but gets an opportunity here to put that right. Tonight he is below his last winning mark of 70, and that gets him into a 0-70 handicap where previously running in 0-75. This horse has 'magic' Oisin Murphy on board and looks to have a very big chance.
Little Keilee ran two good second places since joining the in-form James Owen yard, then ran a right stinker the other day, finishing last of all. I think a bounce back is in order.

Rich Rhythm was unsettled at the start in his last race back in May, rearing in the stalls. He won over course and distance in the race before and could bounce back if his stable has settled his problem.

Thortonledale Max blew the start and had trouble in running on his first start for six months when 4th at Lingfield last time. He needs a decent start from stall 1 but should go close anyway with luck in running.
Veteran who has been running well this spring after returning from 15 months off the track and went close over course and distance in April. Should be capable of striking soon.
Ernie's Valentine won off 71 last December. His last three runs have been below par, and his mark is now 70, which gives him an EW chance today.

Profitman is a 4-year-old gelding trained by B F Brookhouse. He is a three-time winner on the AW and a dual CD winner and has won off marks of 47-51-55. He has course form of 3-1-2-2-6-1, so he really loves this track. He currently runs off 65, so some 10lb higher, but has shown he is capable off this mark given his shd 2/9 at Newcastle on penultimate start behind Cusack off a mark of 64 under today's jockey Billy Loughnane, posting a career-high RPR of 72. Cusack has since won another two races to bolster the form and is 10/40 wins on AW. B F Brookhouse ran one horse at Chelmsford in July 24 on the 07/07/2024 - Cardano won at 40-1 - Profitman is drawn well in stall 3 - outside chance. B F Brookhouse also picked x
up a further 3 winners at Chelmsford in 2024 and is 5/27 in 2024/2025 - outside chance if stripping fit.

In receipt of weight from others here. Little competition from the others in terms of form. Winner of Point-to-Point bumper and then second here 19 days ago. Likely to build on that win and a fair play although odds on. JJ Hanlon trained. Promising 4yo.

The 5yo was a decent 3rd on his bumper debut, the race won by a decent type. He can return stronger today after 13 months off the track. The small yard are flying at the moment, 13 winners for a 23% strike rate in the last two months. He can be a big player in this weak looking NHF flat race.

The model I run suggests Schmilsson can win this one. Schmilsson lines up here with the highest RPR of the group but looks well treated off this official ranking. Goes out carrying quite a bit less weight than Aspire Tower, where the weight differential is close to 1 and a half stone. Schmilsson comes here in reasonable form, having won the last 2 on the bounce, with the latest of those coming 23 days ago. Race fitness should not be a concern. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which has been driven by the small gap back to second in the race simulation. This translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Two runs this year for the 8yo mare, and two wins from two over fences. Looking good last month when winning by 7L - high RPR rating posted. No problem with the quicker ground. Her main rival got lucky last time out when the clear leader fell at the last.

Has his 2nd run for this yard today. Looked to hold every chance last time out when unseating rider at the final obstacle. He's still quite lightly raced over fences. Just 6 runs to date. To be fair, he registered both his chase wins in the spring, with both of those chase wins coming in stronger races than this one. Firstly, he beat the short-priced favorite Westport Cove at Wexford, with not much separating them at the line. That form looks better now with the runner-up winning a beginners chase easily on his most recent run. His most recent chase win came on his final run for his former stable. He won a novice chase off a huge weight very easily. The standout chase form he possesses came at Thurles. He was only beaten 9 lengths by subsequent 3-time Grade 1 scorer Il Etait Temps. He's the one to beat on that form alone here. Yard are in fine form at the moment.
This race should prove a stiff task for this Kerry Lee horse. It has good hurdles form and, although it is off the handicap, could go well on chase debut.

The Jamie Snowden trained Doc McCoy is the last of Jamie's 3 runners on tonight's card. He won well at Ffos Las in a conditional jockeys race under Izzi Ryder, and followed up without a penalty when winning last time out at Fontwell. The handicapper has given him a 12lbs hike in the weights but Izzi takes 7lbs off here. He is unexposed over this trip and hopefully he can continue his good form.

Just six starts over hurdles for the 7yo, he has a win and has been a close runner-up twice. He went very close on his handicap debut a year ago - solid looking form. He was a decent 3rd four weeks ago and should be ready for a big run. On a decent mark, should be fine on the quick ground and he has a strong jockey in the saddle.

The model I run has suggested Getalead could win this one. Getalead lines up here with the highest RPR of the 9-runner field and doesn't look overly penalized for it in the weights. Comes here having shown some form when placing in 3 races on the bounce, the last of those coming only 10 days ago. Needs to show a bit more to get over the line first, but having only raced 10 days ago, race fitness shouldn't be a concern. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which has been driven by the small gap back to second in the race simulation. This translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
Has been coming down in the weights. Didn't like the ground last time out at Worcester. Headgear back on today and well supported as a good outsider's chance.

Jack The Savage's form has dropped off lately. He has only won one bumper and one hurdle race in 27 races under rules. However, he had four 2nds and three 3rd places in hurdle races and could get at least a place, dropped to a mark of 97 with Kevin Brogan back on board.

Realistic Optimism is the second of Jamie Snowden's three runners on the card this evening. Back from a break and after a wind operation, he ran well to be second last time out. Hopefully, he can now start winning over hurdles, and this Class 5 handicap looks like a good place to start.

My other pick is Hill Station, who has run really well twice in a row at Newton Abbot. Luke Scott is riding again. He was a bit unlucky in the run-in last time out, but I still think he would have lost. Should again be there at the end.

Star Legend has had four wins in his last five runs in staying races on the flat. Although he won last December over hurdles, that was over nearly three miles, and he has been going close without winning over shorter distances. He should go close again.

The model I run has suggested Square Du Roule might cause an upset here. This has been driven by Square Du Roule having the second highest RPR of the 10-runner field, but has an official ranking that is the third lowest of the entire field. This subsequently leaves him carrying the third lightest amount of weight around this 2m 2f round trip. The weight differential up to some of the market leaders near the top of the weights is over 1 stone and might be telling by the finish. Has shown some consistent form placing but needs to show a bit more to win. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Just held on last time out at Hereford, beating the hot Henderson favourite. The 3rd horse was 9 lengths further back. Also has good form at this track when 2nd of 12 in a maiden, so worth chancing at 9/1 e/w if eight go to post.

A wind op had little effect this time last year to impact results, but a visor and a 192-day break seems to have had the desired effect. Won with a length to spare at Huntingdon and although bumped up in weight, has won much higher in the past. Keeps the visor here.

Not too many miles on the clock for the 7-year-old, and he is quite consistent. Excuses last time out on his chase debut. Better judged on his previous run when beaten just 3L in a handicap hurdle. The 1st, 2nd, and 4th have given that form a nice boost since. Same mark for this handicap, but a more experienced jockey takes over in the saddle. He looks a little overpriced.

Theonlywayiswessex was caught close to home after a good run, finishing second at Warwick on 4th June, so has had time to recover. He is fancied to win so long as Tom Bellamy can hang on to him a little longer and not go too early like at Warwick. The slightly lesser trip in distance should help too. Each way at 7/2 is our nap.

The 9-year-old was back in form three weeks ago, losing by a short head to a winner who was making it four wins in a row, and he was 14 lengths clear of the rest. He has been 1st or 2nd in 7 of 12 races over fences. No problem with the better ground, on a handy mark and has every chance.

Found 2m 6f too far last time out here at Stratford. Lost two places on the run, dropping back a couple of furlongs today, and has a decent record here at Stratford with form figures of 2, 1, 1, 4. Looks a good e/w bet here at 12/1 if eight go to post.

T Or Coffey was only beaten a length over two and a half miles in a handicap hurdle at Cork in May. He is the most experienced here after six runs over hurdles, to go with fourteen on the flat. Although a long-standing maiden under rules, this looks winnable on his first run for Jennie Candlish.

The 4yo was a good 3rd on his hurdle debut two weeks ago, beaten 5L but only losing out on the run in. The winner that day looks like a decent type. He should be better for the run and this maiden hurdle looks very average.

Chips And Rice ran well at Worcester recently on his hurdle and stable debut. He jumped well and ran prominently in a decent race for the grade but faded near the finish. He was returning from a 252-day break, so probably needed the run. He had some good flat form on good to firm ground, and he gets those conditions today. Ciaran Gethings takes the reins again, and with experience and race fitness under the belt, a better show can be expected today.

St Cuthbert's Cave is a 7-year-old gelding trained by Gordon Elliott. He made an eye-catching chasing introduction when finishing a 3-length runner-up at Kilbeggan behind Aspurofthemoment, who was making a winning chase debut and was winning three races in succession. He is my short-priced banker of the day.
Park The Giant is returning fresh after a break, having shaped well over this trip before. Proven at the distance, with top jockey Brian Hayes reunited and expected to bounce back strongly.
Well-bred sort who made a good impression on debut when placed. Should have come on plenty for that and can prove very hard to beat on reappearance.

This horse was very unlucky when racing at Epsom last time out. Plus, he never liked the course, and he looks well handicapped in this race. He has run very well behind unbeaten Treasure Beach and Fearnot, and on that form, he will go close today.

Lavender Breeze was a promising 3rd place behind stablemate Beyond Dreams at Leopardstown over 7f first time out, where she briefly led on the outside 2f out. She is drawn wide here but should get at least a place.

Malpeque is a 3-year-old filly trained by Gavin Cromwell and owned by Lindsay Laroche. She appears to be highly regarded yet has posted an RPR of just 31 in both starts. She made a seasonal reappearance as a 3-year-old and was heavily backed from 7-2 into 7-4f but finished down the field 8/11, beaten by 17 lengths. She is out of a 96-rated dam, Illumined, with 2/5 wins, and is a second foal and half-sister to five-time winner Snellen (Chesham Stakes (Listed Race) rated 103 and finished 2/23 in the Kensington Palace Stakes handicap at Royal Ascot (owned by Lindsay Laroche). Lindsay Laroche also won the Qatar Prix de Royallieu (Group 2) (3yo+ Fillies & Mares) (Turf) in France with the 104-rated Princess Yaiza and also owned the useful Sunset Shiraz, rated 104. A leap of faith is required with Malpeque but some horses are late developers and could put her best foot forward today under stable jockey Gary Carroll.

Green Rose is a 3-year-old colt. Green Rose is a half-sister to Alessia Fernanda, trained by D K Weld, who won a Cork handicap over a mile off 63 before being moved on and later won off 77 for Declan Carroll, posting a career-high RPR of 84. Green Rose will come on for debut run 6/8 under Leigh Roche. The dam was ordinary, run once, but related to 11/55 wins Tha'ir 109 and 3/7 wins 104. Green Rose has a chance on pedigree.
Was a winner of both of the first 2 races before placing in 3 of the next 4 outings. Not seen since September, but likely to be there or thereabouts if returning in the same form.

Hipop De Loire at 7.50 - 8.00 looks like solid value. He finished a promising fifth in the prestigious Ebor Handicap when last seen, has the top-rated Colin Keane booked, and represents the formidable Willie Mullins.
Romzina's last race (the Orby Stakes) has been franked by the winner and the third place in that race. Still lightly raced and open to improvement, should not be available at such big odds here.

Apercu at 23.00 is an excellent each-way price. She's a rapidly improving mare who has won two of her last three starts, is drawn perfectly in stall 1, and should be favoured by the predicted weak pace.

Soft Winds is in stall 2 with a mark of 108, which looks fair for a steadily improving filly. She was fourth in the Group 3 Munster Oaks Stakes at Cork last time, beaten 5 lengths, which tells me she can compete at a high level. Trainer Joseph Patrick O'Brien and jockey Ryan P Whelan have 18 runs together with an 11% win rate and 28% place rate. She has won twice on similar going, which suits today, and handles this class well. Stall 2 is good for her as she likes to race prominently, and with a solid pace expected, she should get a nice tow into the race. The trainer has a strong record in this race, making her a strong each-way chance despite the tough field.

Sea The Boss is a 4-year-old filly trained by Mrs. John Harrington. She is 2/8 on turf and rated 97, having been rated as high as 101. She is a winner on today's yielding ground and a Group 3 winner at Naas, beating Madam Celeste by a neck, who won a listed race on her last start. Sea The Boss has not been at her best year-to-date, beaten 6 lengths in a listed race on her seasonal reappearance behind Bubblegum at Cork, finishing 7/10. She then finished 6/10 in a Group 3 last time out, with Bubblegum only 1/2 length ahead so she may be coming to hand. Sea The Boss has an impeccable pedigree, being sired by Sea The Moon, rated 122, a three-time Group winner and a winner of the German Derby. Sea The Boss sports first-time cheekpieces today, and Mrs. John Harrington has landed 43 winners in first-time cheekpieces, the last of which won at 50-1 in the Saratoga Special at Ayr, posting an improvement of some 20 pounds. If Sea The Boss takes to the new headgear, we could see a vastly different horse today.
Sidiza certainly looks a good type to capitalize on this mark and the step up in trip here. Has a solid chance for top connections.

Thrifty Of Digby is in stall 12 with a mark of 86, which looks fair to me. She won well by 1 and a quarter lengths off 67 here two runs ago. Last time, she was third, beaten 5 lengths off 70, but went too fast early and tired. Trainer Jessica Harrington and jockey Shane Foley have 19 runs together with a 5% win rate and a 26% place rate. She wears cheekpieces with a good record in them and loves the ground here. Stall 12 is wide, but with a strong pace, she should be able to track the leaders and score here.
Action Plan at 8.00 is a strong value play. He was very unlucky when a fast-finishing second here last time, beaten only a neck after being denied a clear run.
Has had 2 runs for Mullins, both over an inadequate trip. Now upped to a more suitable 10f, and Keane has been booked. Very strong each-way bet here for 4 places.

Useful mare deservedly got off the mark, with a comfortable success of 9 furlongs at Punchestown in September. Raised 7 lbs for that and went up another 4 after just failing to follow up, at Navan. Making seasonal flat return, but ran respectably over hurdles in May. Each way value.

STORMIE OUTLOOK is a mare who seems to be ridden by Seamie Heffernan when she is well fancied. That was indeed the case at this time last year when she racked up back-to-back summer wins and she hinted last time out her turn was near. Workable mark and an each-way play.

I think this 4yo is peaking at the right time. Tactically versatile and has bounced back with two strong runs in deep handicaps. Has upside at this trip, a useful apprentice on board, and looks well-treated. Clear value here.
Vierson at 15.00 presents excellent each-way value. He was a good second over this course and distance last time and is now 4lb better off with the winner of that race.

FIREBRAND is an interesting contender with now scarcely used 7lb claiming apprentice Darragh O'Sullivan coming in for just this sole ride today. As a five year old with his noteworthy sire he could be in peak condition as a racehorse now and feasibly treated back on the level he appeals.

Won this race last year off a mark of 68, beating the top weight rated 82 into 2nd. Races off 63 today, and the top-rated horse here is 80. So why shouldn't this front runner win again? I'm in at 25/1 e/w.

Northern Attitude was a close second over course and distance on her penultimate race for this seven pound claiming rider and she did not run badly when 5th last time but has been dropped a pound to a mark of 60.
In what looks like being an open-looking race, I am going to side with Distillate, who can be a little inconsistent but was 3rd at Fairyhouse recently and could improve on that run to win this.
This one was only beaten 3.5L when 4th with this same 10 lbs claimer on board. As this is her only ride of the day, it's a good value each-way bet for the 4 places available.

Although Clever and Classy is still a maiden after 9 starts, she looks interesting on a couple of recent runs. She was second in an 8-furlong Gowran handicap in May off a mark of 52, and last time was 4th of 17 in a Leopardstown handicap off 55. She led most of the way there until finding the extra furlong too much. Back at 8 furlongs and 2 lbs lower, she looks a good EW bet with 4 places on offer.
Question over whether Roscommon is soft as advertised. But if so, from a low draw and with a handy claimer on, I expect Pimstrel to run better here.

Sunday Sovereign was once trained in England by Tim Easterby, who always said this horse loves soft ground for sure. Has got a long absence to overcome but has done this before. Was 40/1 early doors, so someone knows something on a dreary, rubbish Roscommon Tuesday card. Runs again on the 3rd at Bellewstown. Interesting. E/W nap 4 places.

Dylan Browne McMonagle was in the saddle, finishing in third place at Ballinrobe. This was over nine furlongs. Tonight's trip of twelve furlongs can see Janes Harbour having the stamina to see the trip out. Being a daughter of Camelot, she can put on a good show with progress appearing on the second outing and third run of her career.

Colpe Cross is a 4-year-old filly trained by Miss Natalia Lupini. She has had just the one start and was heavily backed 18-1 into 9-1. Ridden by Wayne Lordan over 10.5f, she raced in the rear, raced wide over 2f out, and made some headway inside the final furlong, but was never dangerous. Today's step up to 12f should suit, and Seamie Heffernan takes the ride. Out of a dam, New Winds, who went 2/5 wins both as a 2-year-old, winning novices at good tracks like Newmarket on debut and Haydock on the third start. Watch the market as she will surely have benefited from the experience. Seamie Heffernan and Miss Natalia Lupini, when combining, are 2/20 in maidens with Making Time 11-4 and Kitty Rose 25-1, and are 5/20 placed. One to keep a close eye on.
Could well build on recent win here over a mile four. Up eight pounds for that, but the step back in trip might just prove ideal in an attempt to follow up.
Flying Fortress did not appreciate the extra furlong at Limerick three weeks ago. The drop back in trip should suit him and give him a chance to bounce back.
Had an off day at Leopardstown last time, but on his previous second at Navan, he'd have every chance today, especially if first-time cheekpieces help unlock extra.
They are stepping this one back up in trip on its handicap debut with the same jockey on board. A good value each way bet.

Small each-way for this horse who definitely needs to find some improvement to get involved but she's very lightly raced so some progress is possible. Didn't have much luck in the run last time, can be forgiven that and possibly worth one more chance.
Has shown glimpses of promise in 3 starts to date. Should be better than those results have shown, and any improvement will give an each-way chance.
